summary: Shortest number of moves to collect all litter in a grid with limited energy and reset tiles.
mainInsight: BFS over states (row, col, mask of collected litter, energy). Each move costs 1 energy; stepping on 'R' resets energy to the maximum; stepping on 'L' sets its bit in the mask. Because there are at most 10 litter cells the mask has at most 1024 values. Prune with best[row][col][mask] = the highest energy seen: a state with no more energy than one already seen is dominated.

promptVariants: Why can a state be pruned when its energy is not larger than a previously seen one?
cards.answer: BFS reaches states in nondecreasing move count, so a later arrival at the same (cell, mask) with energy no greater than an earlier visit is no better: anything it can do, the earlier state can do as well and with at most as many moves. Only a state with strictly higher energy can improve future options.
keyPoints: Earlier visit has fewer or equal moves
